metadata.title: AI sell-off: These sectors held firm as tech slumped in Oct, Nov

content.text:
Investing.com -- Semiconductors, software, and memory stocks fell hard through October and early-November amid mounting questions over the long-term artificial intelligence trade.
But this sparked a rotation into defensive sectors, with healthcare, retail, logistics and REITs either holding their ground or even rising. The sectors also appeared attractive after vastly lagging tech during the AI-fueled surge over the past year.
Where the damage landed
The pain spread beyond chips. Datadog (DDOG) fell 35.1% and Lumentum (LITE) fell 34.9% over the month. Copper miners Southern Copper (SCCO) (-28.8%) and Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) (-28.7%) also dropped. Both are likely hit by the same AI-infrastructure demand narrative, so Materials isn't a clean hedge.
Where money hid
Healthcare looks like the strongest refuge:
-
IDEXX Labs (IDXX): +23.6% over 1M, +27.8% over 3M
-
Edwards Lifesciences (EW): +17.7% over 1M
-
Regeneron (REGN): +14.3% over 1M
-
Becton Dickinson (BDX): +9.7% over 1M, +42.2% YTD
Their earnings don't depend on AI capex, so they gain when money leaves crowded growth trades.
Defensive consumer and restaurants:
-
Chipotle (CMG): +22.4% over 1M
-
McDonald's (MCD): +10.5% over 1M
-
Costco (COST): +10.1% over 1M, +27.6% YTD
-
Target (TGT): +9.5% over 1M
-
Lowe's (LOW): +11.1% over 1M
Several of these had lagged earlier in the year, so part of the move looks like catch-up. The Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) is up 6.1% over 3M and 22.4% over 1Y, with an RSI of 62.3. That is steady rather than explosive.
Industrials, insurance and real estate:
-
UPS (UPS): +12.4% over 1M
-
Aon (AON): +11.8% over 1M
-
Simon Property (SPG): +8.8% over 1M
-
Comcast (CMCSA): +11.2% over 1M
Tech that held
Not all tech fell. Two groups stood out:
-
Motorola Solutions (MSI) rose 12.6% and Roper Technologies (ROP) rose 16.3%. Both sell steady, recurring-revenue products, not AI hardware.
-
AppLovin (APP) gained 39.1% over 1M, but it's still down 43.8% YTD. That is a rebound, not a safe haven.
